title: Dedicated autoscaler: burst controls and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Diego Chen
release_notes: Enhances dedicated autoscaler with smoother token-bucket burst controls, adds per-fleet utilization reporting and new observability metrics. Improves throughput guarantees while reducing transient queueing under bursty traffic. Backwards-compatible config changes; opt-in smoothing defaults enabled for new clusters.
body:
Motivation: Production fleets running Dedicated capacity observed transient latency spikes and unfair burst consumption during short traffic surges. Existing token-bucket burst control was too permissive for priority routing and produced noisy utilization metrics that made capacity planning harder. This PR implements a smoother token-bucket smoothing algorithm, improves burst accounting across priority queues, and adds a fleet-level utilization reporter that exports stable SLO-aligned metrics to Prometheus and internal observability.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces token-bucket smoothing with configurable smoothing_window and decay factor to avoid instantaneous full-burst consumption.
- Adds per-priority burst quotas and cross-priority backpressure to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Implements a fleet utilization reporter service that aggregates per-node effective throughput and token-bucket usage and exposes the following metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_fleet_utilization_ratio, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_consumption_seconds, dedicated_autoscaler_priority_backpressure_events_total.
- Adds end-to-end integration tests for bursty traffic and priority routing.
- Adds a small migration path: new smoothing config defaults to off for existing clusters; cluster-ops can enable via the Dedicated Helm chart values.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/controller.go: core autoscaler logic updated to call smoothing policy and to record new metrics. (~230 LOC modified)
- pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go: new smoothing helpers and thread-safe decay loop.
- pkg/autoscaler/priority_router.go: cross-priority accounting and backpressure hooks.
- obs/metrics/registry.go: new metric registrations and helper for fleet-level aggregation.
- cmd/dedicated/fleet_reporter/main.go: new lightweight reporter binary that aggregates and exports fleet metrics.
- charts/dedicated/values.yaml: new config knobs smoothing.enabled, smoothing.window_ms, smoothing.decay_factor.
- tests/integration/autoscaler_burst_test.go: synthetic load tests to validate behavior.
- docs/release-notes/dedicated-autoscaler-v2.md: release note draft and rollout guidance.

Commits (summary):
- feat(autoscaler): add token-bucket smoothing primitives
- feat(autoscaler): priority quota accounting and backpressure hooks
- feat(obs): fleet utilization reporter and Prometheus metrics
- test(integration): add bursty traffic scenarios and assertions
- chore(charts): add smoothing config to dedicated values
- docs: release notes and rollout guidance

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for token-bucket smoothing and priority accounting. Integration suite includes a deterministic burst replayer that validated queueing and tail-latency under 10k simulated requests; CI initially failed a flaky test (TestBurstPriorityRouting) due to race in the mock clock; fixed by introducing a deterministic clock in tests. Final CI: all checks passed.

Rollout plan: Feature is opt-in. Steps:
1) Deploy fleet_reporter sidecar/daemonset (can be disabled).
2) Enable smoothing in a canary pool and monitor dedicated_autoscaler_fleet_utilization_ratio and priority_backpressure_events_total.
3) Gradually enable smoothing across remaining pools if metrics show reduced burst consumption and no SLO regressions.

Migration notes and compatibility: The change is backwards compatible. Existing clusters will see no behavior change unless smoothing.enabled=true. The metrics are additive and safe to query; names are stable. Helm chart adds new keys and defaults

Related: Linear ENG-3245 (autoscaler smoothing design), ENG-4410 (fleet utilization reporting). Sup ticket SUP-1287 reported customer-visible burst issues that motivated this work.

Review conversation (high-level): reviewers requested careful attention to metric cardinality and memory usage in the fleet reporter, and verification that smoothing does not introduce sustained underutilization. We added aggregation buckets and a small memory cap in reporter; tests added to exercise edge cases. Priya requested clearer telemetry names; renamed a few metrics to the finalized names above.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged on 2026-02-20 after final approval. No rollbacks required during initial canary.

review_comments: Priya Desai: Please ensure fleet reporter doesn't increase metric cardinality; prefer aggregated gauges over per-node labels.
Diego Chen: Agree - changed reporter to aggregate server-side and added a node_count label only for debugging builds.
Mina Park: Does smoothing risk sustained underutilization for low-traffic pools? Can we add a guard to ensure we don't throttle healthy steady-state traffic?
Diego Chen: Added a lower-bound floor (min_rate) and tests that validate no underutilization under steady load.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed on TestBurstPriorityRouting due to race; reproduce locally and added deterministic clock - looks stable now.
Priya Desai: Approved after metric name cleanup and memory cap added to reporter.
